'''Laura Aline Katz''' is an American biologist who is the Elsie Damon Simonds Professor of Biological Sciences at [[Smith College]].

==Early life and education==
Katz was born to Phyllis Beck Katz and Arnold Martin Katz.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gover |first1=Tzivia |title=This Writer's Way |url=https://www.smith.edu/news/saq-fall-2020-patricia-lee-lewis-70 |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=September 28, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Arnold Katz Obituary (1932 - 2016) - Hartford, CT - Hartford Courant|url=https://www.legacy.com/amp/obituaries/hartfordcourant/177465069|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.legacy.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Willerson|first1=James T.|last2=Dhalla|first2=Naranjan S.|date=2016-04-01|title=In Memoriam: Arnold M. Katz, MD (1932–2016)|url=https://meridian.allenpress.com/thij/article/43/2/106/85333/In-Memoriam-Arnold-M-Katz-MD-19322016|journal=Texas Heart Institute Journal|language=en|volume=43|issue=2|pages=106–107|doi=10.14503/THIJ-16-5827|issn=0730-2347|pmc=4845582}}</ref> She earned her [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Harvard College]] and her PhD from [[Cornell University]].<ref name = "smith bio">{{cite web |title=Laura A. Katz |url=https://www.smith.edu/academics/faculty/laura-katz |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
Katz joined the faculty at [[Smith College]] in 1997 where she co-founded Smith’s Achieving Excellence in Mathematics, Engineering and Science (AEMES) program. She also established the Katz Laboratory which focuses on "elucidating principles of evolution through reconstruction of evolutionary trees, community sampling of diverse microorganisms from local environments and analyses of genome evolution."<ref name = "Change">{{cite web |title="Change-Your-Life" Teaching: Three Faculty Members Awarded Sherrerd Prize |url=https://www.smith.edu/about-smith/news/faculty-members-awarded-sherrerd |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=May 4, 2017}}</ref> Katz also began studying the biodiversity of eukaryotic microbes to find eukaryotic life on earth which cannot be seen by humans.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Katamay |first1=Kaja |title=It's a Small, Small, Biodiverse World |url=https://www.smith.edu/insight/stories/biodiverse.php |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=June 20, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q|Q28254627}}</ref>

As an [[associate professor]] of biological sciences, Katz was named to the Biodiversity Science and Education Initiative to examine the deteriorating condition of the earth’s biodiversity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Smith Women Named to Prominent Groups |url=https://www.smith.edu/newssmith/winter2006/newsbriefs.php |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=Winter 2006}}</ref> She later received a five-year $1.2 million grant to closely examine the evolutionary relationships among 200 eukaryotic microbes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Smith College Leads Peers in Decade of National Science Foundation Funding |url=https://www.smith.edu/insight/stories/nsf.php |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=March 11, 2010}}</ref> Katz was also appointed one of 11 principal investigators chosen for the Open Tree of Life project, a project aimed at designing a complete online "tree of life" to represent all life forms on Earth and their evolutionary history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McCoy Ebbets |first1=Jan |title=Building the complete tree of life, microbe by microbe |url=https://www.smith.edu/insight/stories/treeoflife.php |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=December 12, 2012}}</ref>

In 2019, Katz was awarded a $443,222 grant from the [[National Science Foundation]] for her research project "Collaborative Proposal: Combining single-cell ‘omics’ and community analyses to reveal functional and genetic diversity in marine planktonic ciliates."<ref>{{cite web |title=People News, September 2019 |url=https://www.smith.edu/news/people-news-sept-2019 |website=smith.edu |access-date=December 18, 2020 |date=August 29, 2019}}</ref>
